items.followUp: How does chlorine react with hydrogen? Write the balanced chemical equation and name the product.

rubric.why: Fluorine reacts very vigorously or explosively with hydrogen.
rubric.description: Describes how vigorously fluorine reacts with hydrogen.
rubric.how: Accept that the reaction is vigorous, rapid, or explosive.

rubric.why: The reaction forms hydrogen fluoride, HF.
rubric.description: Identifies the product or gives the balanced equation.
rubric.how: Accept hydrogen fluoride, HF, or the balanced equation.

modelAnswer: Fluorine reacts explosively with hydrogen to form hydrogen fluoride.

items.followUp: State any four observations from Rutherford's alpha-particle scattering experiment.

rubric.why: Most alpha particles passed through the gold foil without being deflected.
rubric.description: States that most alpha particles passed straight through the foil.
rubric.how: Accept that most passed straight through or without deflection.

rubric.why: A small number of alpha particles were deflected from their original paths.
rubric.description: States that a few alpha particles were deflected.
rubric.how: Accept that some or a few particles changed direction.

rubric.why: Only a very small number of alpha particles were deflected through large angles or returned backwards.
rubric.description: States that very few particles were deflected through large angles or bounced back.
rubric.how: Accept large-angle deflection, rebounding, or bouncing back.

rubric.why: The large number of particles passing through showed that most of the atom is empty space.
rubric.description: States that the atom is mostly empty space.
rubric.how: Accept equivalent wording that most of the atom's volume is empty.

rubric.why: The scattering showed that the atom has a small, dense, positively charged nucleus containing most of its mass.
rubric.description: Describes the nucleus as small, dense, and positively charged, or states that it contains most of the atom's mass.
rubric.how: Accept the nucleus's key characteristics or that most atomic mass is concentrated in it.

modelAnswer: Most alpha particles passed straight through the gold foil without deflection.
A few alpha particles were deflected from their original paths.
Very few alpha particles were deflected through large angles or bounced back.
Most of the volume of an atom is empty space.
An atom has a small, dense, positively charged nucleus that contains most of its mass.
